summary: Gov. Dan McKee lost the Democratic primary, so no incumbent was on the ballot. Helena Foulkes (Democrat) won, defeating Ken Block (independent) and Aaron Guckian (Republican).

candidates.name: Helena Foulkes
candidates.bio: Helena Foulkes is a former president of CVS Pharmacy and a former chief executive of Hudson's Bay Company. She was the Democratic nominee for Rhode Island governor in 2026, after an unsuccessful 2022 primary run.

positions.summary: Proposes a childcare fund matched by employers, starting with a $20 million pilot, and describes childcare, housing and transportation costs as barriers to work.
Says she would raise Medicaid reimbursement rates to narrow the gap with Massachusetts and Connecticut and take steps to keep eligible Rhode Islanders covered.
Proposes a $100 million bond to build and modernize career and technical education facilities.
Says she would lower energy bills and increase renewable energy production, including a $40 million solar-and-battery program and an audit of Rhode Island Energy.

candidates.name: Ken Block
candidates.bio: Ken Block is a Barrington businessman who founded the government-accountability group Watchdog RI. He was the Moderate Party nominee for governor in 2010, sought the Republican nomination in 2014, and ran as an independent in 2026.

positions.summary: Says he would reduce expenses rather than add taxes, veto a millionaires tax, suspend the truck toll program, and eliminate state income tax on Social Security.
Says he would require hospitals to send one bill after a stay, seek higher Medicare reimbursement rates for Rhode Island providers, and take no actions that undermine the Affordable Care Act.
Says he would push back the state's 100% renewable energy goal from 2033 to 2040 and direct Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative auction funds to energy bill relief for low-income households.
Says on his campaign site that he does not intend to impose his own beliefs on others when it comes to abortion.

candidates.name: Aaron Guckian
candidates.bio: Aaron Guckian ran for lieutenant governor of Rhode Island in 2022 and lost. He has also led the Rhode Island Dental Association. He was the Republican candidate for governor in 2026.

positions.summary: Says Rhode Island's budget is too large ("a $15.2 billion budget for a million people") and that he wants to lower taxes and fees.
Says teachers carry too much administrative burden and that cutting it would let them get back to the basics in the classroom.
Says he voted for the president "in regards to border security."
Disagreed with how the Trump administration moved to halt work on the Revolution Wind offshore wind project, which was 80% complete at the time.
Is described as anti-abortion, and says it is settled state law.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called). Vote totals read Nov. 25 from thegreenpapers.com. Write-ins are in the total. Certification not confirmed.
